title: WAVE-J: Redefining High-Performance JPEG for the 8K Era - Semiwiki
gist: Daniel Nenni details Chips&Media's WAVE-J JPEG codec IP, successor to CODAJ12V: 8K60 encode at 430 MHz and decode at 500 MHz, up to about 2,950 Mpixels/s, 3.5x encode and 2.7x decode gains over its predecessor, 64K x 64K maximum image size, a move to a 128-bit AMBA AXI4 interface, and roughly 18.75 mW encode power in TSMC 7 nm at about 0.05 to 0.1 mm2.

insights.claim: WAVE-J encodes 8K images at 60 frames per second at 430 MHz and decodes 8K images at 60 frames per second at 500 MHz.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The clock-rate-to-throughput figures set the bar competing JPEG IP must clear for 8K-class designs.

insights.claim: Measured throughput reaches approximately 2,950 Mpixels/s for 8-bit 4:0:0 encoding and 2,690 Mpixels/s for 8-bit 4:0:0 decoding, while the widely used 4:2:0 format runs at approximately 2,060 Mpixels/s encoding and 2,020 Mpixels/s decoding.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Format-dependent throughput matters because 4:2:0 is the volume case and shows a roughly 30 percent haircut from headline numbers.
insights.locator: Depending on chroma format and bit depth, measured throughput reaches

insights.claim: Relative to the prior CODAJ12V architecture, WAVE-J achieves encoding gains of up to 3.5 times and decoding gains of up to 2.7 times while retaining compatibility with established JPEG workflows.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A generational step-up large enough to trigger re-licensing by existing CODAJ12V customers.
insights.quote: Relative to CODAJ12V, WAVE-J achieves encoding gains of up to 3.5 times and decoding gains of up to 2.7 times.
insights.locator: Relative to CODAJ12V, WAVE-J achieves encoding gains

insights.claim: Submodule throughput improvements are broad rather than concentrated: pre- and post-processing roughly 3.2 times higher, transform and quantization doubled, variable-length coding improved roughly two to four times, and variable-length decoding improved up to 2.5 times.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Uniform block-level gains suggest a full redesign rather than a targeted tweak, implying durable rather than benchmark-specific advantage.
insights.locator: Submodule throughput has been improved substantially.

insights.claim: Entropy processing has been refined around 8 x 8 block-based operation, increasing sustained throughput and reducing performance degradation for vertically oriented images.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vertical-image performance matters for smartphone and digital pathology workloads where portrait orientation dominates.
insights.locator: Entropy processing has also been refined

insights.claim: A major architectural improvement is the transition from a 64-bit AMBA AXI3 interface to a 128-bit AMBA AXI4 interface, with selectable burst lengths of 8, 16 or 32 transactions improving memory-system efficiency and alignment with modern SoC fabrics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Interface modernization is often the real integration blocker for legacy IP; removing it opens design wins in new SoCs.
insights.locator: A major architectural improvement is the transition

insights.claim: Quantization and Huffman tables can be downloaded through either APB or AXI, reducing control-path bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Control-path flexibility reduces integration effort, a soft but real determinant of IP selection.
insights.locator: Quantization and Huffman tables can be downloaded

insights.claim: A generalized DMA engine supports bitstream concatenation for efficiently encoding images rotated by 90 or 270 degrees, as well as constant-value filling.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rotation handled inside the codec removes a separate processing pass, cutting system-level memory traffic.
insights.locator: A generalized DMA engine also supports operations

insights.claim: Internal memories have been redefined to improve area-to-capacity efficiency, while an optional 28 KB SRAM configuration can increase latency tolerance in memory-constrained or highly contended systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Configurable buffering lets the IP survive in contended AI-server memory systems, broadening addressable sockets.

insights.claim: WAVE-J expands the maximum supported image dimension from 32K x 32K to 64K x 64K, targeted at panoramic imaging, digital pathology, aerial mapping, AI datasets and other workloads processing extremely large still images.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to non-consumer, higher-value verticals as the growth vector for JPEG IP rather than commodity phone cameras.
insights.locator: WAVE-J expands the maximum supported image dimension

insights.claim: The codec supports 8-bit, 10-bit and 12-bit sample paths across multiple planar and packed formats including YUV400, YUV420, YUV422, YUV444, RGB and ARGB, with integrated bit conversion enabling 10-bit input or output even when the JPEG processing path uses 8-bit or 12-bit representations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Format breadth reduces the need for surrounding glue logic and widens the set of SoCs the IP can drop into.
insights.locator: The codec supports 8-bit, 10-bit, and 12-bit sample paths

insights.claim: Integrated pre- and post-processing supports fixed-ratio downscaling by 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32, chroma-format conversion, color-space conversion, arbitrary cropping, mirroring and rotation, which reduces the need for separate image-processing accelerators and minimizes external-memory traffic.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Absorbing adjacent image-processing functions expands value capture per socket at the expense of standalone ISP blocks.
insights.quote: These functions reduce the need for separate image-processing accelerators and minimize external-memory traffic.
insights.locator: The pre- and post-processing pipeline supports fixed-ratio downscaling

insights.claim: In a TSMC 7 nm SVT implementation at 500 MHz, estimated total power is approximately 18.75 mW during encoding and 14.80 mW during decoding for an 8-bit codec configuration with pre- and post-processing enabled.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sub-20 mW at 8K60 makes the block viable in battery-powered edge devices, not only plugged-in systems.
insights.locator: In a TSMC 7 nm SVT implementation at 500 MHz

insights.claim: Depending on configuration the implementation occupies roughly 0.05 to 0.1 mm2, with a full-featured configuration estimated at about 1.03 million logic gates, 16.64 KB of SRAM and 1.33 million total gate equivalents.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Concrete area and gate-count figures let integrators price the block against alternatives and against software JPEG.
insights.locator: Depending on configuration, the implementation occupies roughly

insights.claim: Configuration options let implementers select encoder-only, decoder-only or combined codec functionality, choose 8-bit or 12-bit processing, enable only required preprocessing features, and balance memory capacity against latency tolerance, which helps control silicon area and power across products.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Modularity supports tiered licensing and lets one IP serve both cost-sensitive and high-end sockets.
insights.locator: Configuration options allow implementers to select

insights.claim: Although the full WAVE-J configuration is larger than CODAJ12V, the increased gate count delivers substantially greater throughput and broader functionality, improving performance per integrated imaging task.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The area-for-throughput trade is the pitch; buyers on tight area budgets may still stay on the older core.
insights.locator: Although the full WAVE-J configuration is larger than CODAJ12V

insights.claim: WAVE-J is positioned for smartphones, cameras, surveillance systems, AI servers, edge devices and appliances, and is framed as a compact imaging subsystem rather than merely a standalone JPEG engine.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI servers appearing alongside phones in the target list signals JPEG IP riding datacenter image-pipeline demand.
insights.quote: makes it suitable as a compact imaging subsystem rather than merely a standalone JPEG engine
insights.locator: Bottom line: WAVE-J is positioned for smartphones
